outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said that on Monday, Nov 16, hourly rolling blackouts of 1 to 3 queues for all consumers, plus industrial capacity limits, are in effect around the clock in parts of Ukraine, tighter than Sunday's 1 to 2 queues. UNN, citing Ukrenergo, said one queue is four hours, so Monday's outages may last from 4 to 12 hours. UA.News, also citing Ukrenergo, said the Monday schedules apply throughout the day in certain regions. No later official Ukrenergo Monday schedule change was found. On Sunday afternoon, Ukrenergo said a Russian attack damaged energy equipment and that emergency power outages had been introduced in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, said Sunday evening that power supply had been restored in the Zaporizhzhia region after the attack, according to Ukrinform at 9:00 p.m. EET. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found for the Dnipropetrovsk emergency outages. DTEK said some consumers in the cities of Dnipro and Kamianske, and in the Dnipro and Kamianske districts, were left without power, that crews were restoring supply where the security situation permitted, and that it did not give a customer count. Kamianske mayor Andriy Bilousov, in a Sunday evening update reported by 5692.com.ua, said outage schedules were not in effect, that electricity was being supplied first to critical infrastructure, that repair crews were working continuously, and that the pace of restoration also depended on security conditions; he gave no customer count and did not say the city had been fully restored. Overnight outages: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said in a Nov 15 statement that a Russian attack overnight on one of its energy facilities left 41,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said crews began work once it was safe, that they were clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment, that restoration will take time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work). Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, also said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility; Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk, and reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found. Prior Saturday outages with no later official restoration notice found: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on one of its facilities in the north of Odesa region on the morning of Nov 14 left almost 50,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly and that air-raid alerts were complicating the work). On Nov 16, SUMYTODAY, citing Sumyoblenergo, said part of Sumy region was still without a stable electricity supply for a second day after an accident at a high-voltage facility; the utility said the damage was too complex for a quick return of power to all customers and that backup feeding was significantly limited because of ongoing Russian attacks on energy infrastructure (no customer count). On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found.

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: Almost 50,000 customers without power, according to DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. Crews began work once it was safe, clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly, that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work, and that restoration will take time. No restoration time was given. This is a separate Nov 14 attack from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found for this Nov 14 outage.

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: 41,000 customers without power, according to a Nov 15 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack overnight on Nov 15 hit one of its energy facilities, that 41,000 customers were left without electricity, that crews began work once it was safe, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment, clearing rubble, and making repairs, that restoration will take a long time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work. No restoration time was given. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk; reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power and that six people were injured. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found.

outages.place: Mariupol, Donetsk, Volnovakha, Novoazovsk, and nearby cities
outages.cause: Occupation authorities described an emergency in the regional power system. The Russia-appointed head of the Donetsk occupation government, Andrey Chertkov, said the grid was damaged by a "powerful enemy attack," while some Russian media called it an accident. Vedomosti reported that Ukrainian forces struck energy infrastructure in the region overnight Nov 15
outages.affected: No official customer count was given in the Nov 15 statement by the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, which said there was a partial power outage in the Donetsk, Mariupol, and Dokuchaevsk urban districts and in the Novoazovsk, Telmanove, and Volnovakha municipal districts. The ministry said crews had begun emergency restoration work and that, if conditions were favorable, a phased restoration of supply was planned by night. It also said that because of a shortage of capacity in the regional power system, supply was being limited in a number of districts, including parts of the Shakhtarsk municipal district, and that power would be restored as the system stabilized and technical conditions allowed. Vedomosti, citing the same ministry, also said that after overnight strikes on energy infrastructure, morning outages on Nov 15 had already left parts of Donetsk's Petrovskyi district, the Snizhne urban district, one settlement in the Amvrosiivka district, and part of the Yenakiieve urban district without power. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, citing Chertkov, said the first substations might return to service overnight, while other occupation authorities, including the ministry, said the damage was extensive and that it was not yet possible to determine when power would be restored. In a later Sunday evening statement carried by dnrnews.ru at 8:18 p.m. local, Chertkov said the damage was serious, that it was difficult to say how long restoration would take, and that by a preliminary estimate substations could be re-energized no earlier than 2:00 a.m. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found. (RFE/RL also attributed a figure of more than 120,000 subscribers in Donetsk to the Russia-appointed mayor, Alexey Kulemzin; that figure matches a separate Nov 11 Kulemzin statement and was not included in the Nov 15 ministry statement, so it is not used here as a current count.)
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026, occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy statement via dnrnews.ru 5:01 p.m. local (= 8:01 a.m. CT) and Vedomosti; RFE/RL / Radio Svoboda report dated Nov 15; Chertkov Sunday evening statement via dnrnews.ru 8:18 p.m. local (= 11:18 a.m. CT); rechecked 11:58 PM CT Sunday, no later official restoration notice found

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns (Santa Cruz unit 1, Antonio Guiteras, Felton unit 2, and Renté unit 3) and maintenance (Santa Cruz unit 3, Nuevitas unit 5, Felton unit 1, and Renté unit 5); thermal generation is also limited by 251 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Sunday bulletin, published by Cubadebate and attributed to UNE-MINEM, forecast 1,860 MW affected at the evening peak: 970 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,830 MW deficit), if the forecast conditions hold. At 6:00 a.m. Sunday, the grid had 925 MW available versus 2,265 MW of demand, leaving 1,340 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,500 MW affected at midday. UNE said Renté unit 3 was expected to add 45 MW at the Sunday evening peak. On Saturday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Saturday affectation was 1,878 MW at 7:00 p.m. Saturday solar photovoltaic output was 3,116 MWh, with a maximum of 485 MW at midday. No official Sunday midday or evening-peak actual was found, and no official Monday UNE national bulletin had been published as of this recheck (early Monday morning in Cuba). On Monday, Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana reported generation-deficit interruptions starting at 12:02 a.m. Cuba time on circuits S513/S515 in San Miguel del Padrón and MB920, and said circuit P317 (25 y K) was restored at 12:03 a.m., according to CiberCuba's Nov 16 compilation. The national grid was not reported as collapsed.

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Homestead Park, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. City Power's Hursthill SDC bulletin issued at 7:30 a.m. SAST Monday, Nov 16, did not list the Mayfair Substation 16-hour emergency shutdown among current outages. The bulletin also did not say that Phase 1 customers (including Mayfair West, the SABC, and Netcare Garden City Hospital), remaining Mayfair-area customers, or Sentech had been restored. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation and stabilise the network after the prolonged outage, affecting those Phase 1 customers, and that Sentech would remain without electricity until multiple cable faults had been located and repaired. SABC News, in a 1:48 p.m. SAST Sunday report, quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena giving the same shutdown details. The planned 16-hour window would have run until 4:00 a.m. SAST Monday; no later official notice confirming that the shutdown had ended, or giving a new customer count, was found. The same Monday 7:30 a.m. Hursthill bulletin said the centre was managing 1,524 open calls, 1,266 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). It said operators were on site investigating an outage affecting Coronationville, Westbury, Newclare, and Paarlshoop, reported Sunday, Nov 15 (no customer count or restoration time). For the Roosevelt Substation (Emmarentia Distributor) outage reported Nov 13, it said restoration was approximately 75% complete, that the fault had been located, that repairs were scheduled that morning, and that customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield would remain without electricity until repairs were complete. It also reported an Industria Substation outage, first reported Nov 11, with service restored to more than 70% of affected customers in Longdale and the test branch assisting that morning in locating the fault so repairs could proceed at two remaining load centres, and a separate Industria transformer fault affecting customers on Kudu Street, reported Nov 13, for which a replacement was still being sourced. In a 7:35 a.m. SAST Monday Roodepoort SDC bulletin, City Power said one load centre at Florida Substation's Mechanical Workshop Switching Station would remain off until repairs were completed for customers in Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia (outage reported Nov 14), that a contractor would be assigned to conduct repairs, and that it gave no restoration time; the bulletin also said loadshedding remains suspended until further notice. At 3:31 a.m. SAST Monday, City Power said 90% of supply had been restored to customers in Bramley View and Corlett Gardens after a Gresswold Substation outage, with the remainder off due to lack of access, and that the outage had been handed to the day shift. Earlier Saturday, City Power had restored electricity to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West after overnight repairs and testing at the Hursthill and Mayfair substations, and said engineers would continue preparing for Phase 2, expected to restore remaining affected customers if there were no further technical challenges. No official Phase 2 completion notice was found. In a Saturday afternoon SABC report, City Power's Noel Maso said parts of Mayfair, Auckland Park, Crown Mines, and Vrededorp remained without power, that restoration and replacement costs stood at R24.8 million, and that in a worst-case scenario it could take up to 14 days to restore power to all affected areas.
outages.etr: No official notice confirming that the Mayfair 16-hour emergency shutdown had ended, or giving a restoration time for remaining Mayfair-area customers or for Sentech, was found; City Power's 7:30 a.m. SAST Monday Hursthill bulletin no longer listed that shutdown among current outages. For the Roosevelt Substation outage in parts of Emmarentia, City Power said Monday morning that repairs were scheduled that morning and that customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield would remain off until repairs were complete. For the Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia outage, City Power said Monday morning that one load centre would remain off until repairs were completed, that a contractor would be assigned, and it gave no restoration time.
outages.updated: Nov 16, 2026, Hursthill SDC bulletin 7:30 a.m. SAST Monday (= 11:30 p.m. CT Sunday) and Roodepoort SDC bulletin 7:35 a.m. SAST Monday (= 11:35 p.m. CT Sunday); Gresswold 90% restoration 3:31 a.m. SAST Monday (= 7:31 p.m. CT Sunday); Mayfair Substation customer alert 12:15 p.m. SAST Sunday (= 4:15 a.m. CT); rechecked 11:58 PM CT Sunday, no later official notice confirming the Mayfair 16-hour shutdown had ended or that Phase 2 or Sentech had been restored, and no official customer count

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026 (Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15); generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 11:58 PM CT Sunday
